broads_reedcutter.text: {greeting} Norfolk reed's the finest thatching reed in the land. Cut in winter when the leaves have dropped, bundled, stood to dry. A good reed roof'll last you fifty years or more.
Cutting keeps the reedbed young, and the bitterns and harriers like it that way. A fen that nobody cuts turns to scrub, then to wood. We're gardeners, really. Wet ones.

then.text: Take a bundle, go on. Crafters are mad for it.

else.text: You've had today's bundle. Come back tomorrow, the reed's not going anywhere.
